- Execution defaults can pin a chat environment as `folder` or `worktree`. Resolve the pin nearest-first across section, ancestors, project, and global settings. A `worktree` pin preselects a managed worktree on the folder host in both New chat and the composer chip; spawn must preserve that managed-worktree selection. With no pin, keep the existing folder/section-provider behavior. Groups must never become chat environments.
- Section placement resolves environments by folder path. When the same folder belongs to an ancestor section and its descendant, bind the chat to the ancestor section. Explicit `thread_places` assignments take precedence. A single matching section keeps existing behavior; sibling sections sharing a folder remain unbound, and a project-root match remains unbound. Apply the shared resolution rule consistently in list bindings, `naturalPlace`, and `locate`.
- Full plugin backups use a versioned JSON payload (`kind: 'bb-project-folders-backup'`, version 1) containing settings and all 11 durable tables: folders, folder_paths, thread_places, folder_rules, project_rules, project_order, execution_defaults, session_policies, preferences, item_styles, and folder_archives. Imports preserve row IDs and run in one transaction; invalid backups and imports during an active move or archive are rejected. Transient tables (exports, pending_exports, project_moves, thread_moves, section_moves) are excluded. This adds no schema changes and preserves the existing appearance-only export/import flow.

The pinned machine inherits nearest-first alongside existing execution groups (provider/model, permission mode, environment mode, and session agent).

1. Execution Model (execution.ts):
`executionSchema` currently defines optional execution configurations: provider/model (`providerId`, `model`, `reasoningLevel`, `serviceTier`), permissions (`permissionMode`), environment (`environmentMode`), and CLI agent binding (`agentMode`, `agentId`). Layers of `ExecutionLayer` (combining `Origin` and `Execution`) are evaluated in `resolveExecution`, which walks layers nearest-first so the closest ancestor defining a group wins. `normalizeExecution` strips fields not owned by active groups so that unpinned groups remain unset. To implement the contract, `executionSchema` must gain an optional machine host ID pin, and `ResolvedExecution` must gain `machine: { hostId: string; origin: Origin } | null`. Inheritance resolution and normalization must handle this new machine group, maintaining existing worktree construction via `managedWorktreeEnvironment(hostId)`.

2. User Interface (execution-ui.tsx):
`ExecutionEditor` loads settings via `rpc.call("execution_read", { scope })` into a `Loaded` record containing `own`, `effective`, `inherited`, `hostId`, `fallback`, and `agents`. The UI renders toggleable rows with switch controls for each execution group. To satisfy acceptance criteria, a 'Своя машина' row with a toggle switch and device select must be added. The select must list available machines for the scope (filtered to hosts where the place has a folder, or all hosts at global scope). When switched off, the row displays the inherited origin via `originLabel`. Changes are persisted via `rpc.call("execution_save", { scope, value: normalizeExecution(draft) })`.

3. Session Startup and Fallback (composer-chip.tsx, section-tree.ts, section-environment.tsx):
When starting a new session from the composer chip or the New chat screen, the session must resolve the effective machine host and folder path. If the pinned host does not have a folder for the place, it must fall back to the home host. When combined with an environment pin (`folder` or `worktree`), the target environment must reflect the pinned host.

4. Invariants and Compatibility:
Places without machine pins must maintain 0.6.28 behavior. Existing stored records and backups must load without error.
